q.t: Most of the water on Earth is…
q.e: Almost all of it is ocean water, which is salty.

q.t: If all the Earth's water were a 200 ml glass, the freshwater would be about…
q.e: Only about 5 ml out of 200 ml — a tiny part of all water is fresh.

q.t: Ice turning into water is called…
q.e: Heating ice turns it to water — melting.

q.t: Water turning into vapour is called…
q.e: Heated water changes into invisible water vapour.

q.t: Water vapour turning back into water is called…
q.e: Cooling vapour turns it back to liquid — condensation.

q.t: Water stored deep under the ground is called…
q.e: Rain soaks down through soil and rock and is stored as groundwater.

q.t: Rivers, lakes and ponds hold…
q.e: Water on the surface of the land is surface water.

q.t: Fish breathe using…
q.e: Gills take oxygen dissolved in water.

q.t: Lotus and water lily are…
q.e: Their roots are in the pond bed; leaves and flowers float on top.

q.t: Water always flows…
q.e: Water flows downhill, following the shape of the land.

q.t: Why can't we drink seawater?
o: Its salt makes the body lose more water
q.e: The body must pass out the extra salt dissolved in water, so drinking seawater dries you out.

q.t: Water drops appear on the outside of a steel glass holding ice. Where do they come from?
q.e: The cold glass cools the air touching it; cool air can't hold as much vapour, so it condenses on the glass.

q.t: A saucer of water in sunlight disappears in three days. What happened?
q.e: Water that vanishes has always gone somewhere — here, into the air as vapour.

q.t: Why does a city full of concrete get less groundwater?
q.e: Rain runs off paved surfaces into drains instead of sinking into the ground.

q.t: Which surface lets rain soak in best?
q.e: Soil has gaps between its particles for water to sink through.

q.t: Johads in Rajasthan are…
o: Small earthen dams that help rain recharge groundwater
q.e: They catch rainwater and let it seep down.

q.t: Why doesn't a lotus leaf get soaked?
q.e: Like crayon wax on paper, the coating makes water roll off.

q.t: Which river in India reaches no sea at all?
q.e: The Luni ends in the marshy Rann of Kutch because there's no downhill path to the sea.

q.t: Keibul Lamjao in Manipur is special because it is…
q.e: It is made of floating mats called phumdis and is home to the Sangai deer.

q.t: Mist on a window in winter is an example of…
q.e: Warm, moist air touches the cold glass and the vapour turns to droplets.

q.t: The water cycle keeps going forever. Does that mean water is unlimited for us?
o: No — it may not be here, now and clean when we need it
Yes — we can never run short
Yes — the cycle creates new water
q.e: The total never falls, but the cycle takes time and doesn't put water where and when we want it. That's what a drought is.

q.t: In the sealed-bag experiment, droplets form on the upper inside of the bag. This shows…
o: Water evaporates and condenses, recycling itself
q.e: Nothing gets in or out, yet water moves — it is recycled, not created.

q.t: Why does a fish die in air and a dog drown in water?
o: Each breathing organ works in only one medium
q.e: Gills need water around them; lungs need air. Each animal is built for its habitat.

q.t: Mustard seeds poured on crumpled paper collect in the low bits. What does this model?
o: Water collecting in hollows to form lakes
q.e: Like the seeds, water follows the land's shape and collects in low places.

q.t: Why do some Indian rivers flow to the Bay of Bengal and others to the Arabian Sea?
o: The land slopes different ways from where they start
It depends on the rain colour
q.e: A mountain ridge sends rain down one side or the other.

q.t: In a pond food chain, the small fish are removed. What happens to the big fish?
q.e: Every arrow is 'is eaten by'; the big fish lose their food.

q.t: Wular Lake helps prevent floods by…
o: Storing extra river water during heavy rain
q.e: It holds the extra water so less rushes downstream.

q.t: Hiware Bazar in Maharashtra became 'water-positive' through…
o: Rainwater harvesting and careful water use
q.e: Saving rain and using water carefully refilled its groundwater.

q.t: A water scorpion lives underwater but breathes…
o: Through a tail tube reaching the surface
q.e: Its tube works like a snorkel to the air above.

q.t: Why does a pond heron have long thin legs?
q.e: Long legs keep its body dry while it wades and hunts fish.

q.t: Two raindrops land a metre apart on a mountain ridge. They can end up in seas far apart because…
o: Each flows downhill on its own side of the ridge
q.e: The ridge divides the land's slope; each drop follows its own downhill path.

q.t: A city keeps pumping groundwater out while paving more land. What will happen?
q.e: Taking out more than goes in can only end one way.

q.t: Why is 'the Earth has plenty of water' a dangerous belief?
o: Very little of it is fresh and usable
There is no water at all
q.e: It has plenty of water but very little we can drink or use.

q.t: Ocean water is still useful because…
o: It is home to sea life and feeds the water cycle
q.e: Seas support huge life and their evaporation gives us rain.

q.t: Which change needs cooling?
q.e: Vapour → water and water → ice both need cooling.

q.t: Water hyacinth is a problem in ponds because it…
o: Floats freely and spreads very fast
q.e: It drifts and multiplies fast, covering the water.

q.t: A change anywhere in a food chain affects…
o: Both those above and below it
q.e: Remove one link and the change travels in both directions.

q.t: Over long times, flowing water…
o: Wears away and reshapes the land
q.e: Rivers carve valleys and gorges in the land they flow over.

q.t: The fishing cat has partly webbed paws. This helps it…
q.e: Webbing helps it swim — an adaptation for wetland life.

q.t: Dew on grass in the morning forms because…
o: Cool grass makes vapour in the air condense
q.e: At dawn the cool surface turns invisible vapour into droplets.
